walkthrough: Identify the given quantities: start with velocity $u$, end with velocity $v$ after time $t$ with constant acceleration $a$.
State the governing rule for uniform acceleration: $a = \frac{\text{change in velocity}}{\text{time}} = \frac{v-u}{t}$.
Multiply both sides by $t$ to get the velocity change: $at = v - u$.
Rearrange to make $u$ the subject by subtracting $at$ from $v$: $u = v - at$, which is equivalent to $v = u + at$.
Compare with the distractors: options with $at^2$ fail unit homogeneity because $a$ in $\text{m s}^{-2}$ times $t^2$ in $\text{s}^2$ gives $\text{m}$, and options with $2at$ double the true change.
The rearranged equation $u = v - at$ matches the listed equation. This is option B.
